H0001.text: IF we attach a global-count auxiliary head that pools the fine feature map and the exemplar mean and adds a scaled soft-count bias onto the density output IN the CountingHead decoder of the frozen DINOv3-ConvNeXt-Tiny champion THEN final val MAE on FSC147 is at least 0.30 lower than the plain decoder BECAUSE a global count anchor disambiguates scale between sparse and dense scenes, an ambiguity that per-box exemplars cannot represent, so the decoder avoids systematic undercount. DISPROVED IF final val MAE is not at least 0.30 lower than the plain decoder

H0006.text: IF we add a dilated-context branch that runs a parallel dilated depthwise convolution over the fine feature map IN the FineFuser of the CountingHead THEN final val MAE is at least 0.40 worse than with the branch absent BECAUSE dilated context reuses the same exemplar-aligned evidence at a coarser scale, adding redundant cues that the density decoder then double-counts, which raises false positives in dense regions. DISPROVED IF val MAE with the branch is not at least 0.40 worse than without it

H0007.text: IF we read the backbone density-relevant features from its final layer only instead of the intermediate stages 2 and 3 IN the Backbone readout of the champion counter THEN final val MAE is at least 1.00 worse than the intermediate readout BECAUSE final-layer features collapse high-frequency detail needed for precise localization while intermediate ones retain it, and the frozen network never adapts that choice back, so count and localization both degrade. DISPROVED IF val MAE with the final-layer readout is within 1.00 of the intermediate readout

H0009.text: IF we pool the fine feature map globally and emit one scalar gating coefficient that reweights the exemplar tokens per feature channel IN the Condenser of the CountingHead THEN final val MAE improves by at least 0.30 over the unconditional condenser BECAUSE a per-exemplar channel-gain lets the decoder express count-dependent attention that a fixed affine readout cannot, steering the condenser toward scale-consistent exemplar weights.
